title: IETF OAuth charter adds authorization of automated agents
detail: charter-ietf-oauth-06 adds complex delegation: mechanisms or extensions for automated agents that act for users, including across administrative domains. At IETF 127 (2026-11-18 and 2026-11-20) the working group heard several individual agent drafts and adopted none (as of 2026-11-21).

title: MCP specification revision 2026-07-28 released
detail: The protocol becomes stateless: no initialize handshake or Mcp-Session-Id header, and servers must implement server/discover. The release candidate came out on 2026-05-29.

title: A2A becomes a hosted project of the Agentic AI Foundation
detail: The Linux Foundation directed fund that also hosts MCP; A2A's own post calls it a Growth Stage project.

title: MCP Python SDK discloses an OAuth credential redirection flaw
detail: Advisory GHSA-qx49-fqc8-xw99 (high): a malicious or compromised MCP server could steer the client's OAuth credentials to an authorization server of its choosing; fixed in mcp 1.30.0 and 2.2.0. The TypeScript SDK published an advisory for the same flaw class on 2026-09-30 (GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h). An SDK flaw, not a protocol change; GitHub's global advisory database listed the Python advisory on 2026-11-19.

title: Sierra announces Personal Agent Protocol with Meta
detail: An open standard for how a personal agent finds a company, starts a session and signs its user in; first industry partners Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart.

title: OpenID Foundation group publishes a threat classification for agents that cross trust boundaries
detail: From the Artificial Intelligence Identity Management (AIIM) community group: threats that arise when an agent crosses from one domain to another, traced to treating an agent as if it were a human user, with a call for controls at authorization time. A threat model, not a specification.

title: World deprecates and archives AgentKit
detail: Repository marked deprecated (pull request 44) and archived, with no replacement named; by 2026-11-14 the docs overview answered 404 and the integration page redirected to Agent Pass.

title: IETF charters DAWN, a working group on agent discovery
detail: Discovery of Agents With Names, in the Internet Area. At IETF 127 on 2026-11-19 it reviewed candidate drafts, among them DNS for AI Discovery, which Agent Name Service v2 uses by default; it had adopted no working group draft on 2026-11-21.

title: Web Bot Auth working group draft -01 posted
detail: Every Signature-Agent value becomes an HTTPS URL that the verifier fetches directly as a JWK Set; the directory, jwks_uri and cimd types are removed. Deployed signers and verifiers still use the earlier string form.

title: Cloudflare adds per-agent controls for personal agents
detail: AI bot policies renamed AI Crawler and Agent access policies, with Allow, Block on pages with ads or Block for each supported personal agent and a Personal Assistants traffic category.

title: Cloudflare announces the Trusted Agent Delegation coalition
detail: Meant to examine existing protocols and bring well-defined problems to the IETF; World's post of 2026-11-12 presents it as a Cloudflare and World coalition. A whitepaper, no specification or member list (as of 2026-11-14).

title: MCP moves to a six-month release cycle
detail: Releases generally on the last Tuesday of March and September; the next revision is targeted for 2027-03-30, a plan rather than a release.

title: OpenID Foundation lists an Agent Auth (AAuth) working group
detail: Chartered to write specifications for agent identity and authorization across trust domains, with payment protocols out of scope. Its first meeting, set for 2026-11-30, is to decide whether to approve the scope, confirm an editor and adopt drafts; the charter's target dates are plans.

title: Personal Agent Protocol 1.0 released
detail: Sierra announces version 1.0 with more than 100 design partners and a UCP extension that Shopify co-authored; the project's changelog dates the frozen 1.0 text 2026-11-14. The core specification does not cover payments yet; through the UCP extension, payment runs in UCP checkout.

title: KYAPay token draft -04 posted
detail: Pairwise identifiers must now differ at each Target rather than at each Target service, tokens may be kept for audit or dispute resolution, and issuer records are described. Presented at the OAuth working group at IETF 127 on 2026-11-18; no adoption call followed.

title: Personal Agent Protocol starts draft 1.1
detail: Labeled unfinished and not meant for implementations yet; 1.0 stays the version to build against. Draft 1.1 so far recommends that a personal agent also sign its requests to the authorization server with its Web Bot Auth operator signature. On 2026-11-16 the project folded its Path to 1.0 page into the introduction, whose design partner list has 102 names.

title: SD-JWT VC clears its last IESG DISCUSS
detail: After revision -27 (2026-11-16) the ballot stands at 1 Yes and 11 No Objection with no DISCUSS. The draft is still in IESG Evaluation (AD Followup), not approved and not an RFC (as of 2026-11-21).

title: Web Bot Auth session at IETF 127 discusses replacing the web-bot-auth tag
detail: Room consensus for a defined boolean signature parameter in place of the tag, and a sense in the room for a fixed minimum signed set that servers cannot extend; both still need confirmation on the mailing list. No -02 had been posted on 2026-11-21, so -01 still requires the tag.

title: MCP Events extension enters Beta
detail: SEP-3415 merged with status Final, which puts io.modelcontextprotocol/events in the Beta stage: event types delivered by polling, a long-lived stream or signed webhooks, for revision 2026-07-28 onward. No new MCP specification revision; the next one is still targeted for 2027-03-30.

title: MOLE BoF at IETF 127 favors forming a working group
detail: Show of hands on forming a working group from the draft charter: 62 yes, 4 no, 2 no opinion (107 present). BoF polls are not binding; MOLE was still a BoF, not a chartered working group, on 2026-11-21.

title: HTTP working group weighs a draft on 402 semantics
detail: draft-nottingham-httpbis-402-00 would define 402 generically, with no registries or headers; its slides list x402, h402, L402 and draft-httpauth-payment, the MPP core draft, as existing uses. A show of hands on interest in adoption gave 15 yes, 3 no and 18 no opinion (75 present); adoption would need a call on the list.

title: IETF agentproto posts its first working group draft
detail: The Agent Communication Protocols working group, chartered 2026-10-08, is to define a dialog management protocol whose context MCP and A2A could carry with their own mechanisms; changes to those protocols stay with their maintainers. The use cases and requirements draft followed its IETF 127 session of 2026-11-16.
